A0267.title: Rolling-Code and Challenge-Response Access Authentication
A0267.definition: Use one-time rolling codes, randomized challenge-response exchanges, and credential-key authentication so captured wireless access-control or remote-control signals cannot be reused directly.
A0267.description:
Rolling-code and challenge-response access authentication replaces fixed-code remotes, easily cloned low-security RFID cards, and long-lived wireless unlock commands. A rolling-code design keeps synchronized counters at the transmitter and receiver and generates a different encrypted code for each operation. A challenge-response design has the reader issue a random value and the credential compute a response with a protected key, while the receiver validates the key, counter, random challenge, validity window, and device identity.

Deployments should use publicly reviewed modern cryptography and sufficiently long keys, unique per-device keys, secure key injection, failure limits, tightly controlled resynchronization windows, credential revocation, and abnormal-entry alerts. High-value areas should also combine two-factor access, staff verification, anti-tailgating facilities, and access-event auditing so that one wireless credential is not the sole authorization factor.
A0267.limitation: Rolling codes do not inherently stop RollJam-style attacks that combine jamming and capture, and an overly broad resynchronization window can be abused. Challenge-response systems can still be exposed to relay attacks, key extraction, reader replacement, or supply-chain key leakage. Legacy fixed-code equipment often cannot be upgraded in place and requires replacement of both credentials and receivers, creating transition risk while old and new systems operate together.
